Guidance & outlook: We began FY27 on a positive note with total income increased to INR466 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR400 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year, representing a growth of 16.4%.
Our total income for Q1 FY27 stood at INR466 crores as compared to INR400 crores in the Q1 FY26, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 16.4%.
I believe that in terms of the EBITDA guidance of about 14% that we give, we feel confident that we will remain with that kind of guidance and apart from the drop of the retail business.
Growth & demand: We are pleased to report an EBITDA of INR40 crores for the quarter compared to INR33 crores in the corresponding period of last year, registering year -on-year growth of 22.3%.
Profit after tax for the Q1 FY27 stood at INR11 crores as against INR5 crores in the quarter 1 of financial year '26 representing a year -on-year growth of 144.4%.
We have given a guidance earlier in the last quarter of about approximately 12% revenue growth with a 14% kind of EBITDA margin with a drop of 150-odd basis points of the retail business.
Margins & costs: Consumer spending also remained value conscious, while inflationary pressures on the input costs persisted during the quarter, influencing purchasing decisions across segments.
We have already given an indication of an annual drop in EBITDA by about 150 basis points.

And sir, my second question is, if I look at our P&L for this quarter, if I exclude the INR24 crores, INR25-odd crores that we spent on developing the land, the margin seem to be much better from the core operations that we have around 9% to 10%.
Capex & expansion: All this expansion is funded through internal accruals.
The capital expenditure that we had envisaged for this year, as indicated earlier, was close to about INR100 crores with about INR40 crores to INR50 crores going into the retail project.

As we mentioned earlier, the capex for the year is about INR100 crores and even after that and the other dividends and other things, there will still be a positive surplus of cash flow that the company will have in the end of the year.
Balance sheet & cash: The growth is largely due Siyaram Silk Mills Limited July 31, 2026 to operating leverage playing out.
Our debt-to-equity as on 30th June '26 stood at 0.24.
